findings.reason: this is the same wiring gap an earlier review raised for §19 and the author closed by adding f-tmref-005; without a followup naming §20, the next coordinator has nothing to dispatch and the chain reads as finished.
findings.text: `_document` moves §20 to `implementable` but carries no followup naming its invocation: the two open followups are f-tmref-004 (§7) and f-tmref-005 (§19), and §19 is now `done`, so the invocation chain ends on a completed section and §20 has no entry point.

findings.reason: a worker implementing this clause literally removes the per-file identities and reintroduces the stale-snapshot bug the cited code documents, which the node's own gate (a scan count) cannot catch.
findings.text: §20's Deliverable says "The change token is built from directory stamps of the review stores, not from per-run globs", but `_review_input_identities` (`reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:387`) carries per-file identities precisely because a directory stamp cannot see an in-place rewrite, and `reckon/crew/review_records.py:1512–1517` says so in its own comment ("A record rewritten in place … keeps its name, its inode and the store's entries, so the directory's stat identity does not move"); `_crew_home_change_token` (`reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2977`) also states the token must carry "the classification's own composition rather than a cheaper subset of it". A directory-stamp token would leave a rewritten review record unread, so a quiet beat would serve a stale classification — the exact defect the per-file identities exist to prevent.

findings.reason: the named mechanism cannot remove the profile's largest surviving entry, so the node would land a correct per-tick listing and leave the ~30% unchanged; the fix the evidence supports is threading the tick's pointer set into `_declared_head_keyed_record`.
findings.text: §20 names `_review_store_record_paths` among the functions that "read the per-tick listing rather than globbing per run", but that function (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:50–86`) performs no directory listing at all: it walks `node.write_paths` and compares paths. The 30% the profile attributes to it comes through `_review_record_delivery_directory` → `_resolved_reviewed_run_id` (`recovery_review_delivery.py:228–269`), which calls `list_live(project=project)` when `_declared_head_keyed_record` calls `_review_store_record_paths` without `pointers=` (line 121), and otherwise falls through to `run_store.runs_for_node` — a durable-store read, not a store-directory scan.

findings.reason: memoising `resolved_tick_config` in that thread (the stated deliverable) changes neither call site, so the third limb of the deliverable is unimplementable as written.
findings.text: §20 says "The obligation sweep thread also still re-parses the flight YAML per run through `resolved_tick_config`", but the obligation sweep's two flight reads call `flight.resolve` directly and never reach `resolved_tick_config`: `reckon/crew/obligations.py:2770` (`_obligations_view`) and `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1292` (`_derive_fleet_state`). Each is also resolved once per session view or derivation, not per run.

findings.reason: a worker can satisfy the stated bound without reducing any GPFS traffic, and the gate would pass on the unfixed code, so the negative control measures nothing.
findings.text: §20's measure bounds `os.scandir`/`glob` at "most once per review-store directory", but `_review_input_identities` lists a per-run directory — `committed/<project>/<COMMITTED_RUN_DIRNAME>/<run_id>` (`recovery_memo.py:418–421`) — so 40 live pointers permit 40 listings under a literal reading, which is what the base arm already does. The negative control also only says the base counts are "recorded", not that the head assertion fails there.

findings.reason: the sweep-thread memo can fail or land independently of the tick change, so one verdict cannot close the node and one gate proves neither.
findings.text: §20 carries three independently closable deliverables: the producer tick's per-tick review-store listing for `_review_store_record_paths`/`_review_input_identities`/`_own_review_record_exists`, the change token's construction, and a `resolved_tick_config` memo in the obligation sweep thread — the last in a different thread with its own measure (`flight.resolve` per sweep) and no dependence on the first two.

findings.reason: the section's only end-to-end evidence of the cost falling is unopenable, and §19 set the precedent of naming the pre-landing reading's path.
findings.text: §20's post-landing check ("the coordinator samples the live producer's main thread every 2 s for 120 s and records the busy share, against the 54 of 57 recorded before this section") names no durable path for the new samples or for the pre-landing reading it is compared against, so the comparison cannot be re-read by anyone but the coordinator who took it.

findings.reason: the other frame names the same call site and the mechanism rests on them, so correcting the frame spelling would not change what the node does.
findings.text: the §20 profile leg `_snapshot_reuse_key > _classification_inputs > _review_input_identities > select_wildcard / _own_review_record_exists` names `select_wildcard`, which resolves to no function anywhere in the repository (`grep -rn select_wildcard` returns only this plan line), so a reader cannot check that half of the profile.

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §20's bound "at most once per review-store directory" is ambiguous and holds at base on the per-run committed-tree reading, so the negative control cannot distinguish the fix.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §20 names `_review_store_record_paths` as a per-run globber, but it performs no listing; its 30% cost is run-id resolution, which a per-tick store listing does not address.
